sites: Exact new row / Platform matrix and harness cell

mustFix.finding: The row owns and claims leftover closure for EE-5b, but its harness is only a 'hostile-but-well-formed excluded-form admission corpus' and its retained evidence is only 'refused at admission; no ExecutionId'. The frozen v5 source defines EE-5b as a represented PlanIntent, manifest, or protocol-frame substitution after admission but before any stage, with the pass 'rejected before any stage executes'. V1-slice section 7 item 8 makes the two fates explicitly disjunctive: an initially excluded PlanIntent creates no ExecutionId, while a substitution after admission is rejected before any stage. An after-admission EE-5b case cannot be proven by an admission-time no-ExecutionId result. EE-4 also retains an explicit post-admission substitution limb. As written, the exact live row would not specify the corpus or evidence needed to close EE-5b, yet Decision item 5 says that class is closed to G29 execution.
mustFix.impact: Applying the exact MF-6 would install a required gate whose evidence cell does not own one of the seven classes it purports to close. The act's arithmetic would be mechanically correct but the EE-5b leftover-closure statement would be unsupported.
mustFix.repair: Keep one gate if desired, but make all three row cells preserve the temporal split. The claim should say admission/pre-stage validation refuses represented excluded forms. The harness should include both hostile well-formed admission cases and post-admission/pre-stage substitution mutations. The evidence cell should say that admission-time excluded forms are refused with no ExecutionId, while represented post-admission substitutions are rejected before any stage, citing v1-slice section 7 item 8. Then re-review the exact row and Decision item 5 together.

shouldFix.title: The EE-1 claim uses an ambiguous slash instead of the source contract's exact trust predicate
shouldFix.finding: EE-1 admits a publisher that is first-party or explicitly trusted and rejects an otherwise well-formed request only when the publisher is neither first-party nor on the explicit-trust list. The proposed live claim says 'non-first-party/untrusted publisher'. Read as alternatives, that phrase would reject an explicitly trusted third-party publisher merely for being non-first-party; read as a compound label, it reaches the intended case. A live gate claim should not leave that product boundary to slash interpretation.
shouldFix.impact: The class ID and pinned source make the intended predicate recoverable, so this is narrower than D157-MF-1, but the exact file-08 row would otherwise be ambiguous about a deliberately allowed category.
shouldFix.repair: Replace 'non-first-party/untrusted publisher' with 'publisher neither first-party nor explicitly trusted' (or an equally explicit Boolean formulation) in the exact row.

summary: OBJECT at 1 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The three-limb mechanics are otherwise sound: D-156 authorizes this later work, G29 is unassigned, the exact row has eight cells, the live condition-4 before operand occurs once with no backslash bytes, same-act naming is present, and an in-memory application produces 29 gates, 29/29 owners, 25/25 required names, 26 OPEN and 3 HARD-BLOCKED while condition 4 remains MET. The act correctly leaves EE-7a/EE-7b/EE-7d leftover, leaves EE-6b/EE-7c/EE-7e unnamed, keeps DR-117 ineligible and not SATISFIED, restores neither G17 nor G13, invents no D9 code, and authorizes no implementation. The exact G29 row is not yet semantically adoptable, however. It claims EE-5b closure while specifying only an admission-time corpus and 'refused at admission; no ExecutionId' evidence. EE-5b exists after admission and must be rejected before any stage; v1-slice item 8 explicitly distinguishes those fates. The row must name post-admission/pre-stage mutation cases and retain their distinct evidence. Separately, EE-1's 'non-first-party/untrusted publisher' should be replaced by the unambiguous source predicate 'neither first-party nor explicitly trusted'. Custody and all cited digests hold.
